scan.summary: This is Cascade Specialty Chemicals' written emergency action plan for its Portland facility covering fires, chemical releases, medical emergencies, earthquakes, and other emergencies. The plan describes alarm signals, evacuation routes and assembly points, employee accounting procedures, first aid and rescue duties, and a training and review cycle for all 42 employees, contractors, and visitors. The plan is stored in the front office and warehouse break room and is available to employees on request.
scan.freshness_note: The plan was last revised February 2021, now over 5 years old. Oregon OSHA requires annual review every January (Section 6); the document states 'The facilities lead reviews the plan every January.' No evidence is provided that a January 2026 review occurred. A current version should be prepared or the last review date confirmed.

gaps.title: Missing documentation of annual review completion
gaps.description: The plan states the facilities lead reviews it every January, but there is no evidence provided that this annual review actually occurred in January 2026 or any year since the 2021 revision. OSHA requires employers to review and update the plan; lack of dated evidence creates a compliance gap.
gaps.fix: Maintain and provide dated records showing completion of the January 2026 review (or most recent review), documenting what was checked, any changes made, and sign-off by the facilities lead. Keep these records with the plan.
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

gaps.title: Missing employee emergency report procedures
gaps.description: The plan describes what to do when an alarm sounds but does not specify how employees report an emergency in the first place — whether by pulling a manual alarm, calling 911, calling an internal number, or notifying a supervisor. This is a required element.
gaps.fix: Add a section specifying the method by which any employee can report an emergency (e.g., pull manual fire alarm at any exit, call 911, call internal emergency coordinator at extension __, notify supervisor). Make clear that anyone can initiate the alarm.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(1) requires the plan state 'procedures for reporting fires and other emergencies'
gaps.locator: not in the document; should be added as new subsection in Section 1 or 2

gaps.title: Missing identification of emergency coordinator or incident commander
gaps.description: The plan mentions 'the incident coordinator at the assembly point' (Section 4) but never formally designates who holds that role, what training or credentials they need, or their responsibilities during the event. The role is implied but not defined.
gaps.fix: Add a section naming the primary and alternate incident coordinators (by title, not personal name, to allow for turnover), their role and authority, their responsibilities at the assembly point, and their duty to coordinate with emergency responders.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(c) requires identification of persons responsible for directing evacuation and rescue
gaps.locator: not in the document; should be added to Section 1 or new section
gaps.quote: the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire department on arrival

gaps.title: Missing procedures for accounting for persons at other locations
gaps.description: The plan accounts for employees, contractors, and visitors at the building assembly point (Section 4), but does not address how to account for drivers or employees away from the facility (e.g., at customer sites, on the road). It is unclear whether drivers are included in the headcount or how their status is tracked.
gaps.fix: Add language explaining how drivers and off-site staff are accounted for — e.g., 'Drivers and off-site employees contact the facilities lead by phone immediately after emergency. If unable to reach the facility, they report to the designated assembly point or shelter location.' Reference the visitor log and daily sign-in sheet process, and clarify who maintains this log during an emergency.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(c)(2) requires procedures for 'accounting for all employees'
gaps.quote: At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out.

gaps.title: Incomplete designation of trained first-aid responders
gaps.description: Section 5 states there are 'two trained first-aid responders per shift, named on the warden roster' but the warden roster (Appendix B) is not provided in this document. Without seeing the roster, it cannot be verified that first-aid responders are actually named or that they exist for all shifts.
gaps.fix: Ensure Appendix B (Floor warden and first-aid responder roster) is complete, current, and includes the names and shift assignments of at least two trained first-aid responders for each shift. If the company operates multiple shifts, ensure coverage for all of them. Keep the roster posted beside each evacuation map and update it whenever roles change.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(e) requires designated and trained employees; 1910.38(c) requires procedures for rescue and medical duties
gaps.quote: First aid is given at the assembly point by the trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster)

gaps.title: No documented training records or drills
gaps.description: Section 6 describes when training occurs (new employee orientation, annual floor warden/first-aid responder training, review when plan changes) and that drills occur twice a year in spring and autumn, but the document does not show evidence that training has actually been completed, that employees have been signed off, or that drill logs exist with dates, times, evacuation speeds, and corrective actions.
gaps.fix: Maintain and retain: (1) dated sign-in sheets or training records for each employee's initial orientation and any subsequent review; (2) drill logs for each twice-yearly exercise showing date, scenario, duration of evacuation, accountability results, and any issues found; (3) records of annual certification for floor wardens and first-aid responders. Make these available to Oregon OSHA on request.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(f) requires review of the plan with employees; 1910.38(e) requires training; Oregon OAR 437-002-0042 requires documentation
gaps.quote: Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on what is in the document and what is missing from the regulatory standpoint. I am certain that: (1) this is a policy document subject to 29 CFR 1910.38 and Oregon OAR 437-002-0042; (2) it covers evacuation, alarm, assembly, accountability, and training as required; (3) it lacks written procedures for how an employee reports an emergency, identification of the incident coordinator role, and procedures for accounting for off-site/driver staff; (4) no supporting documentation (training records, drill logs, rosters) is provided with the plan itself; (5) the plan is now 5+ years old and the annual January review requirement cannot be verified. I am less certain about: (1) whether the company is actually subject to an EAP requirement (depends on whether another standard triggers it—hazmat handling likely does, but not stated in the plan); (2) the exact content of Appendices A and B, which are referenced but not provided; (3) whether supplementary fire prevention plan or chemical-specific procedures exist elsewhere. The interpretation of 'incident coordinator' as a compliance gap is inferred from the plan's use of the term without definition; some might argue that role is self-evident from context.
